questions.explanation: Past condition, present result: 'would + infinitive'.
questions.q: If you had taken the earlier flight, you ___ home by now.

questions.explanation: Present condition, past result: 'would have + past participle'.
questions.q: If I weren't allergic to cats, I ___ that kitten yesterday.

questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past perfect condition + 'would + infinitive' for a present result.
options: If she had trained harder, she would win now.
If she trained harder, she would have won.
If she had trained harder, she would won now.
If she had trained harder, she will win now.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: A general present condition uses 'were', even with a past result.
questions.q: If I ___ you, I wouldn't have lent him the money.

questions.explanation: The missed practice is in the past, so the condition needs the past perfect.
questions.q: I would be fluent by now if I ___ practicing every day.

questions.explanation: A past action not taken needs the past perfect in the if-clause.
questions.q: If they ___ the contract last year, they'd be our partners today.

questions.explanation: A present wish about the past: past simple in the condition, 'would have' in the result.
options: If I would have more time, I would finish the report.
If I have more time, I would have finished the report.
If I had had more time, I would finish the report.
If I had more time, I would have finished the report.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: Past condition, present result: 'would + be'.
questions.q: She ___ managing the team now if she hadn't taken that career break.

questions.explanation: The storm was yesterday (past perfect), but the result is now: 'would be lying'.
questions.q: If the weather hadn't been so awful, we ___ on the beach now.

questions.explanation: The purchase happened in the past, so the condition needs the past perfect.
questions.q: We wouldn't be in debt if you ___ that expensive car.

questions.explanation: A past action needs the past perfect: 'If you had studied harder'.
options: If I'd known you were ill, I'd have visited.
If I were you, I wouldn't accept.
If you studied harder, you would have passed.
If we'd left earlier, we'd be there by now.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: Birth is a past event, so the condition needs the past perfect.
questions.q: If I ___ born a decade earlier, I'd have seen the band live.

questions.explanation: The trait is general/present, so use past simple 'were' with a past result.
questions.q: He wouldn't have failed if he ___ naturally confident.

questions.explanation: Past condition, present result: 'would + infinitive'.
questions.q: If the company had gone bankrupt, hundreds of people ___ their jobs now.

questions.explanation: Past condition + present continuous result: 'wouldn't be rushing now'.
options: If I didn't oversleep, I wouldn't be rush now.
If I wouldn't have overslept, I wouldn't be rushing now.
If I hadn't overslept, I won't be rushing now.
If I hadn't overslept, I wouldn't be rushing now.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: Past condition (not wearing it), present result: 'wouldn't be'.
questions.q: You ___ in hospital now if you'd worn your seatbelt.

questions.explanation: The offer was in the past: past perfect condition, present result.
questions.q: If she ___ the job in Dubai, she'd be earning twice as much today.

questions.explanation: The cancellation happened earlier, so the condition needs the past perfect.
questions.q: They'd already be home if their flight ___ cancelled.

questions.explanation: A hypothetical past result needs 'would', not 'will'.
options: If we'd invested in tech stocks, we'd be rich now.
If I spoke French, I could have helped them yesterday.
If they weren't so noisy, the baby would have slept.
If he had apologized, she will not be angry now.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: The degree was unfinished before last month: past perfect in the condition.
questions.q: If I ___ my degree, I'd have applied for that position last month.
